units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 4:5:2">Y. Shebi. IV, 35ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>מקום שנהגו לקוץ יִתּוֹק לִתּוֹק וכ׳</he> where it is customary to cut the reeds, let him pluck them; where it is customary to pluck them &c.; <cite ref="Tosefta Shevi'it 3:19">Tosef. ib. III, 19</cite> Var. <he>יִתּוֹךְ לִתּוֹךְ</he>.

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 8:6:2">Cant. R. to VIII, 6</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Jeremiah 22:24">Jer. XXII, 24</cite>) <he>שהוא נוֹתֵק מלכות וכ׳</he> that he will tear the Davidic kingdom out of his hand; <cite ref="Jeremiah 22:24">ib.</cite> <he>משם אני נותק וכ׳</he> from there I shall tear loose the kingdom &c.; Pesik. Shub., p. 163ᵃ.

Bekh. 33ᵇ נותק he who tears loose (testicles and throws them away); נותק אחר כורת who removes them after one has cut them (tearing off the roots). Sifra Thazr., Neg., ch. VII, Par. 5 אם נְתָקוֹ אדם if a man made it bald (נֶתֶק); (R. S. to Neg. III, 5 אם נִיתְּקוּ בידי אדם, Nif.); a. e.—Part. pass. נָתוּק (b. h.) an animal whose testicles have been forcibly removed; [oth. opin.: whose membrum has been mutilated by a violent severance]. Sifra Emor, Par. 7, ch. VII; Tosef. Yeb. X, 5.

<cite ref="Tosefta Terumot 3:13">Tosef. Ter. III, 13</cite> <he>ענבים רכות ונוֹתְקוֹת … ואינן נוֹתְקִין וכ׳</he> grapes are soft and let their juice ooze out (when packed), but olives are hard and do not let their oil ooze out.; Y. ib. III, 42ᵇ top, v. <cite ref="D00496"><he>דֵּיהֶא</he></cite>.

senses.gloss: to tear loose. Cant. R. l. c. (ref. to Jer. l. c.) אֲנַתֶּקְךָ אין … אֲתַקֶּנְךָ it does not say ănatteḳkha (I shall tear thee loose), but (it may be read) athaḳḳenkha (I shall restore thee, v. תָּקַן); Yalk. Jer. 303 אַתֶּקְךָ (Hif.); Pesik. l. c.

units: <cite ref="Sifrei Bamidbar 115">Sifré Num. 115</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 750:13">Yalk. Num. 750</cite> <he>התחיל הבן ההוא מְנַתֵּק</he> that son began to protest (against doing slave’s work); <he>התחילו ישראל מְנַתְּקִים</he> the Israelites remonstrated (against the laws imposed upon them); v. infra.

senses.gloss: to be torn loose; to fall out.
units: <cite ref="Chullin 123b:19">Ḥull. 123ᵇ</cite> <he>שומר העשוי לִנָּתֵק מאליו</he> a protection (cover) which it likely to come off of itself.
<cite ref="Niddah 65a:23">Nidd. 65ᵃ</cite> <he>כיון שנִתְּקוּ שניו וכ׳</he> when a man’s teeth are gone; a. e.

senses.gloss: [to tear one’s self loose,] to remonstrate, be discontented. Sifra Aḥăré, Par. 9, ch. XIII גלוי … לִינָּתֵק בעריות it was known before the Lord that they would bear unwillingly the restrictive laws concerning sexual relations; נִיתְּקוּ בעריות they did remonstrate &c. (ref. to Num. XI, 10; v.
units: <cite ref="Shabbat 130a">Sabb. 130ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Yoma 75a">Yoma 75ᵃ</cite>); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 590">Yalk. Lev. 590</cite>.

<cite ref="Zevachim 5b:14">Zeb. 5ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>אשם שנ׳ לרעיה</he> an animal dedicated as a guilt-offering which (on account of its owner’s death &c.) has been condemned to pasture until natural death (v. <cite ref="O00003"><he>סָאַב</he></cite>).—Y. Naz. IV, end, 53ᶜ <he>משנ׳ מלא תעשה לעשה</he> since it (the cutting of the hair which is forbidden to the Nazarite) has gone over from a prohibition to a positive duty (<cite ref="Numbers 6:18">Num. VI, 18</cite>).—<he>לאו שנ׳ לעשה</he> a prohibition transformed into a command, i.e. a prohibitive law the transgression of which must be repaired by a succeeding act, e.g. (<cite ref="Leviticus 19:13">Lev. XIX, 13</cite>) ‘thou shalt not rob’, and (ib. V, 23) ‘he shall make restitution.’ <cite ref="Chullin 141a">Ḥull. 141ᵃ</cite> (for which <cite ref="Mishnah Chullin 12:4">ib. XII, 4</cite> <he>מצות לא תעשה שיש בה קום עשה</he>).
<cite ref="Yoma 85b:13">Yoma 85ᵇ</cite> <he>לא תעשה שנ׳ לעשה</he>; a. fr.

senses.gloss: (v. Kal 2) to enter a stage of moist decomposition. Y. Naz. VII, 56ᵇ, v. נֵצֶל.—5) (denom. of נֶתֶק) to become hairless and blanched, to be afflicted with נֶתֶק.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Negaim 10:9">Neg. X, 9</cite> <he>ונ׳ כל ראשו</he> and his entire head became bald (v. <cite ref="S01984"><he>קָרַחַת</he></cite>). Sifra Thazr. l. c. <he>את שני׳ נתק בתוך נתק</he> a person that became afflicted with a bald spot within a patch of hair surrounded by baldness (<cite ref="Mishnah Negaim 10:7">Neg. X, 7</cite> <he>שני נְתָקִין זה לפנים מזה</he>; a. fr.).
